name: Amcha Yisrael
spread: 0–8 — too new for pollsters to agree; i24 has shown it as high as 8
note: New party — bloc placement and red lines not yet confirmed
desc: Launched 25 August 2026 by a retired IDF brigadier general who commanded the Givati Brigade. Pitches itself as a broader, less sectarian right than Otzma Yehudit or Religious Zionism. Netanyahu has warned publicly that it splits the right-wing vote.

positions.annex: Right-wing on territory; the party has not published a detailed platform.

cautions.text: Winter has said Amcha Yisrael seeks a broad right-wing government with 'Zionist partners', which reads as ruling out reliance on Ra'am — but he has not said so outright.

name: The Reservists
spread: 4 — has only just started clearing the threshold in polls
note: Newly merged list — red lines carried over from Zionist Home, worth re-checking
desc: Yoaz Hendel's party, founded in 2025 out of a post-October 7 movement for reserve soldiers and their families. Ran as Zionist Home with Chili Tropper until the two split in September 2026 — Tropper joined Yashar, Hendel kept the party and merged with Yaron Zelekha's New Economic Party, adding an economic platform to a security one.

positions.annex: Supportive of settlement but has not pushed for formal annexation.
positions.draft: Supports a broader, more equal draft — the party's founding issue is the burden carried by reservists.

refusals.text: Hendel has ruled out sitting with the ultra-Orthodox parties over the draft-exemption fight.
Hendel has ruled out sitting with the ultra-Orthodox parties over the draft-exemption fight.

cautions.text: Hendel's party has been cool toward relying on Ra'am's votes — unlikely, but not ruled out.

_why: Dissolved 6 Sep 2026. Chili Tropper left to run with Yashar; Yoaz Hendel kept the party, which merged with the New Economic Party and now polls as The Reservists (see above). No longer a column in Wikipedia's table.
